mentions.name: Reverse typesetting
mentions.description: Reverse typesetting tool that reflows page layouts for documents whose typesetting structure is unknown, such as scanned physical books or PDF papers. It infers layout using naive rules-based heuristics on bounding-box dimensions and gaps, then reflows the pages to fit e-ink readers. Built in Common Lisp, targeting an Emacs mode for interactive execution with manual feedback.
mentions.problem: Scanned physical books and PDF papers have fixed page layouts with unknown typesetting structure, so their content cannot be reflowed for resizing to e-ink readers.
mentions.audience: The author's own use — reading on a pocket-sized e-ink reader carried around ("User #1 is me").
mentions.source_excerpt: Reverse typesetting: reflowing page layouts where you don't have knowledge of the typesetting structure, i.e. a scanned physical book or PDF paper. Naive rules-based heuristics based on the dimensions of bounding boxes and gaps. Point is to reflow things for resizing to eink readers. (Specifically the size that fits in my pocket which I carry around. User #1 is me). Building in Common Lisp and targeting an Emacs mode for interactive execution with manual feedback.
